a: Linnane, William, d. 1826? author Linnane, William

IE12459753.c: Irish Gaelic poems of William Linnane and others, compiled by E. O'Curry. 1823. Purchased in 1867 from the Melbourne antiquarian bookseller and publisher Henry Tolman Dwight. This and RARES 091 C76 are companion volumes, written by the same unidentified scribe, and presumably with the same O'Shanessy provenance. Matter on page 136 indicates associations with Eoghan Ó Comhraidhe (Eugene O'Curry), while indebtedness in matter of script and contents to the scribal work of Éinrí Mac an tSaoir is noted in the description of RARES 091 C76. MS 10357 is a miscellany of prose and verse, the prose consisting of the story of the Children of Lir. The poetry consists of a mixture of eighteenth-century Munster verse, Ossianic poetry, some items of Ulster poetry, and at least one item ('Tír na nGrásaigh', page 120) associated with a printed source contemporary with the manuscript (see Colm Ó Lochlainn, 'Literary forgeries in Irish', Éigse: a Journal of Irish studies 2/2, 1940, pages 123-36). ; 1 volume, 124 pages. IE23679844.t: Letter from Eliza Newton to an unidentified male, [1883]
a: State Library of Victoria. State Library of Victoria.
IE23679844.c: This letter is dated 30 June 1883, is addressed to an unidentified male, and replies to an enquiry after a map (of the land taken up by John Batman around Port Phillip), that had been in the possession of her late husband. It having been acquired by him before 1840 from the sale of the effects of John Batman, for whom he was one of the executors. The writer affirms her belief that the map was original (rather than a copy), because she had had in her possession a paper signed by Indigenous persons ceding the land to Batman, but which she believes was destroyed. This letter replies to an undated one from Robert Russell in the Autograph Collection. ; 2 p. (0.1 cm). ; Batman, John, 1801-1839
